request.spec:
When a grade has no rate in force on a date on a sheet nor on its parents, a sheet that was
cloned uses the rate of the sheet it was cloned from (and so on up that sheet's parents and
source).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When a grade has no rate in force on a date on a sheet nor on its parents, a sheet that was
cloned uses the rate of the sheet it was cloned from (and so on up that sheet's parents and
source).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've made the change: a cloned sheet now falls back to its source sheet's rates. The main test ("clone source rates") passes, and so does scenario 2. Scenarios 1 and 3 still fail, and I don't think the spec allows them to pass.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V106__sheet_cloned_from.sql`, adds a `cloned_from` column to `sheet`. `SheetCloner` now fills it with the source sheet's id when it makes a clone.
- **Rate lookup:** `RateRepository` has a new `lineage(sheetId)` method. It gives the sheet's parents first (up to the existing 3 levels), then the sheet it was cloned from, then that sheet's parents and its own source, and so on. No sheet appears twice and the sheet itself is never included, so loops can't happen. Rate lookups for a date, as-of rate lookups and the rates endpoint (`RespondWithRates`) all use it. Due amounts, rollups and statements pick it up through the same lookups.
- **Front end:** no logic change was needed, because it already works through whatever levels the server returns. I only updated the doc comments in `rates.ts`.
- For a sheet that was never cloned, the lookup is exactly the old parent chain.

**The two failing scenarios**
- **Scenario 3** fails at spec line 1212. It expects `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `__SHEET__-p`, which looks like a placeholder that was never filled in. Lines 238 and 1351 make the same check, so scenario 1 would also fail at line 238.
- **Scenario 1** fails earlier, at line 155: it expects a 25.00 claim to be refused, and the app accepts it. That scenario never clones a sheet, so this change doesn't affect it. I didn't dig into it further because line 238 would fail anyway.

**Running `bin/e2e` on this machine:** your shell has `PORT=3002`, and another process (not this app) is already listening on that port. A plain `bin/e2e` therefore can't start this app, and the tests run against that other server and all fail. Use `PORT=3000 bin/e2e`. I left the process on 3002 alone.

While debugging I briefly added a debug spec under `e2e/specs/` and deleted it afterwards. The real spec is unchanged.
